messages.subject: Re: selectAdjacentEdges
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mark,

You are right, this method is needed.

In the meantime, here is a quick hack -- not guaranteed to always work.

Try it out like this:

 1) Manually select a couple of nodes in your CytoscapeWindow
 2) selectEdges (get.adjacent.edge.names (cw, getSelectedNodes (cw)))

It works for me, in a small test.

I will put this on the todo list.

 - Paul

get.adjacent.edge.names = function (cw, geneIDs) {
  all.edge.names = cy2.edge.names (cw@graph)
  all.edge.names.cyStyle = as.character (all.edge.names)

  indices.of.edges.with.geneIDs = c ()

  for (geneID in geneIDs) {
    geneID.regex.nodeA = sprintf ('^%s ', geneID)
    geneID.regex.nodeB = sprintf (' %s$ ', geneID)

    indices.A = grep (geneID.regex.nodeA, all.edge.names.cyStyle)
    indices.B = grep (geneID.regex.nodeB, all.edge.names.cyStyle)

    indices.of.edges.with.geneIDs = c (indices.of.edges.with.geneIDs, indices.A, indices.B)

    } # for geneID

  return (as.character (all.edge.names) [indices.of.edges.with.geneIDs])

} # get.edge.names

messages.subject: Re: Rcytoscape question: "connection reset by peer"
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nicos,

I found this general explanation:

  Connection reset by peer" specifically means that, as far as the application reporting the error is
  concerned, the other endpoint sent a TCP reset packet. Sometimes, both endpoints report this error,
  in which case something in the middle has sent reset packets to both ends. It's not possible for the
  endpoints to get any more information than this.

I can think of a few things to try, in increasing order of fuss:

  1) In the Cytoscape plugins menu, choose the CytoscapeRPC dialog, and make sure that it is 'enabled'
  2) From python, or using wget (I will look up my notes) do a test, outside of R, of the XMLRPC
     server in Jan's plugin.

The plugin and RCy are pretty robust these days, so I think we will find that fixing some TCP problem will fix this.

Let me know, please, how #1, above, goes.  I will check my notes for the lower-level debugging strategies.

 - Paul

messages.subject: Re: Rcytoscape question: "connection reset by peer"
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nicos,

RCy and CyRPC do communicate, by default on localhost, unless you do something special (which you are not).

Try this:
> print (CytoscapeConnection ())
  An object of class "CytoscapeConnectionClass"
  Slot "uri":
  [1] "http://localhost:9000"

You should see the same result.

A while ago, facing a similar problem, we finally learned:

  Yes. I found the problem and sorted that as well. The corporate firewall block loopback on
  localhost/127.0.0.1 <http://127.0.0.1> from certain programs (funny I don't understand why only certain programs are blocked).
  So i have to add exceptions to my firewall to allow loopback on '127.0.0.1'  for R.exe. Another thing to mention is firewall mostly
  allow larger port  numbers (5 digit eg 23333 or so ) than 4 dig (I have no idea why ? ) when starting Cytoscape RPCXML.

Perhaps something similar is happening for you?

 - Paul

All good!

Mark
